html:
The New Deal was the set of programmes that President Franklin D. Roosevelt launched in the United States from 1933 to fight the Great Depression.

After the Wall Street crash of 1929, banks failed, farm prices collapsed and about a quarter of workers had no job. Roosevelt promised "a new deal for the American people" and, in his first hundred days, pushed a flood of laws through Congress. People often sum up its aims as relief, recovery and reform.

  • Relief: the Civilian Conservation Corps and the Works Progress Administration gave millions of people paid work on roads, parks, schools and art.
  • Recovery: the Tennessee Valley Authority built dams and brought power to a poor region; farm laws raised crop prices.
  • Reform: deposit insurance made bank savings safe, and new rules watched over the stock market.
  • The Social Security Act of 1935 created pensions for the old and pay for the unemployed.

Full recovery came only with spending for the Second World War. But the New Deal changed what Americans expected their government to do.
sum: The New Deal was the set of programmes that President Franklin D. Roosevelt launched in the United States from 1933 to fight the Great Depression.
